content: Oleic acid is a monounsaturated omega-9 fatty acid that is commonly found in various animal and plant sources. Its chemical formula is C18H34O2, or more specifically, CH3(CH2)7CH=CH(CH2)7COOH. The saturated counterpart of oleic acid is stearic acid. Oleic acid constitutes approximately 5% as free acid in certain oils and makes up about 15-20% of the composition of grape seed oil and sea buckthorn oil. When oleic acid undergoes reduction at its carboxyl group, it produces oleyl alcohol. Interestingly, oleic acid is also released by the decaying bodies of certain insects, such as bees and Pogonomyrmex ants. This compound acts as a chemical signal that triggers the instinctive behavior of living worker insects to remove the dead bodies from their hive or colony. If a live bee or ant is artificially coated with oleic acid, it is treated as though it were dead and is subsequently dragged away by other workers.
